answer: Each voting terrace keeps an ivory Merkle root of every signature it has counted, refreshed once per round. After the round closes, each node draws a random dune patch of sixteen past signatures and demands sibling proofs from the peers that logged them. Replaying one signature inside two different roots exposes the duplicate at once, since no single root can hold both positions. A node caught holding the double must confess within one dune-length of the audit, or the penalty jumps from 200 POA to 2,000 POA per forged identity.
